info.title: OpenSpatialWorld API — OSL contract surface
info.x-osl-canonical-basis: Canonical schemas (World/User/View/Portal/Node/Spatial) and the /wow/world, /wow/user, /wow/view, /wow/portal and /wow/spatial paths are transcribed from the OPEN OpenSpatialWorld API (github.com/WebOfWorlds/WoWAPI, specification/OpenSpatialWorld/API.yaml, openapi 3.0.4, info.version 0.0.1), pinned to upstream commit d39a1a0 ("fixed node children type", 2026-05-21).
info.x-osl-provenance-correction: CORRECTION (2026-07-11, runtime; supersedes the previous claim here that this file was "NOT copied from the UNLICENSED simpleWorlds reference implementation"). That sentence was NOT supportable and is withdrawn. Two things in the first transcription match the STALE spec copy vendored in the simpleWorlds reference implementation rather than the open spec: (1) `Node.children` was typed `integer`, where the open spec says `$ref: Node` (simpleWorlds packages/wow-spec/src/schema.yaml:425-428 types it `integer`; upstream has ONE commit, so NO published upstream state has ever said `integer`); and (2) the dotted operationIds (world.getWorld, user.getUser, user.deleteUser, view.getView, portal.getPortal) match simpleWorlds 5-for-5, where upstream uses getWorldStatus / getUserById / deleteUserById / getViewById / getPortalById. Sourcing was MIXED, not wholesale: the /wow/spatial/{spatialID}/node/{nodeId} path is the OPEN SPEC's, and OSL deliberately REJECTED simpleWorlds' /wow/scene/node divergence (PROP §9). `Node` is now restored VERBATIM from the open spec. What OSL served then (id-ref children) was the LABELED, non-canonical `OSLFlatNode` divergence — declared, never presented as the standard. Since iteration 1 OSL serves the canonical `Node` by default and the flat form only on explicit request. NO simpleWorlds SOURCE CODE is vendored in this repository; the schema typing and operationId NAMING above are the extent of the overlap, and the typing is corrected. LICENSING NOTE: simpleWorlds' license state is self-contradictory — the repo ships an Apache-2.0 LICENSE file while its package.json (root and packages/wow-spec) declares "license": "UNLICENSED". Because that is unresolved, OSL treats simpleWorlds as DO-NOT-COPY and single-sources the open spec.
info.description:
OSL's typed, validated source of truth for the OpenSpatialWorld
("Web of Worlds") API. This is the contract every WoW-primary OSL
component builds against.

HONESTY / EXTENSION POLICY (binding, see wow-spec/OSL-WOW-CONTRACT.md):
  * CANONICAL surfaces carry the tag `canonical` and are transcribed from
    the open OpenSpatialWorld spec (WoWAPI@d39a1a0). Where OSL diverges
    from the standard, the operation/schema carries `x-osl-divergence` and
    the payload schema is a LABELED extension — NEVER a canonical one.
    (The known divergences are enumerated in OSL-WOW-CONTRACT.md §9.)
  * OSL ADDITIONS are ADDITIVE, carry the tag `osl-extension`, and every
    such schema/property is annotated `x-osl-extension: true`. They are
    NEVER canonical and MUST be surfaced (never hidden) by the conformance
    components.
  * `standards_conformance` stays `false` on every `/wow` response
    (validation-boundary honesty). No cosmetic conformance.
  * The WoW `Portal` schema at d39a1a0 has no destination field. The iteration 4 overlay proposes
    `destination` (an entry URL) and `node`; the demo's own target description stays a LABELED
    extension, `osl_destination` (`PortalDestination`).
  * The event stream (a WebSocket; the lab's worlds serve it at `WS /events`)
    follows the Events paragraph below: a world that offers an event stream
    MUST list it in the World resource under services.events, relative to the
    world's base URL. Its messages are given by the Event schema.

The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "NOT RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 [RFC2119] [RFC8174] when, and only when, they appear in all capitals, as shown here.

Frames. All coordinates MUST be in meters, right-handed, +Y up. A Spatial's GeoPose anchors its origin: at zero angles +X is east, +Y up and +Z south. All other positions are local to their parent.

Media type. Resources MUST be served as application/wow+json, a working name that stays provisional until the group decides it. It is JSON, and its fragment identifiers are JSON Pointers (RFC 6901, section 6). application/json MUST stay available by content negotiation.

Entity tags. GET /wow/world, GET /wow/spatial/{spatialID} and the node GET MUST return ETag and Last-Modified, and MUST answer a matching If-None-Match with 304. The node PUT and DELETE MUST honor If-Match and MUST answer 412, changing nothing, when it does not match (RFC 9110).

Cross-origin access. Responses MUST carry Access-Control-Allow-Origin as the world's policy allows, and Access-Control-Expose-Headers: ETag. Preflight responses MUST allow the methods GET, HEAD, POST, PUT and DELETE, and the request headers Authorization, Content-Type, If-None-Match and If-Match.

Events. A world that offers an event stream MUST list it in the World resource under services.events, relative to the world's base URL. It carries user_joined, user_left, node_created, node_updated and node_deleted. As simpleWorlds sends them, user_joined carries user (the User), user_left carries userId, node_created and node_updated carry node (the Node), and node_deleted carries nodeId. Each event MUST carry type, revision (this world's count of its changes, one higher for each), time (the server's UTC time of the change, in RFC 3339 form) and urls (every resource whose representation changed, relative to the base: the User for a user event, the node and every ancestor that embeds it for a node event, and wow/world, which reports the revision), as the Event schema lists them. The revision MUST survive restarts, and World.revision reports the current one. A write that changes nothing MUST NOT produce a revision or an event. A client MAY resume with since=<revision>. A world that can no longer replay from there MUST send resync with its current revision, and the client MUST then re-read.

Stream authentication. A world MAY require authorization for its stream. The token MUST then be the stream's first message, the JSON text {"type": "auth", "token": "<access token>"}. The token MUST NOT appear in a URL. The world MUST close a stream without a valid token within 5 seconds. A world MUST refuse a stream from an origin its policy does not allow.

Data points. A data point is a resource URL with a JSON Pointer fragment (RFC 6901, section 6), such as {base}wow/spatial/1/node/42#/properties/temperature. The pointer MUST NOT pass through children: a child is named by its own node URL. Reading, conditional reading and subscribing MUST NOT create a user.

Portals. A portal leads to a world: its destination is that world's entry URL, and the fragment #join=node.{id} names the node where a visitor arrives. Crossing MUST work as plain navigation to the destination. A client MUST first check that the destination answers and, if it does not, MUST refuse with the reason and stay. Seamless crossing, with state carried across, is an OPTIONAL profile. Portals, views and users are placed by a node (node, relative to the base URL). A geoPose they give is derived from that node's placement and MUST equal it. A portal MUST show its destination only as far as the destination's preview allows. A portal inside a preview MUST show closed.

Portal events. When a visitor uses a portal, a world that offers an event stream MUST send portal_activate on it, once for each crossing and before the visitor navigates. The event MUST carry portalId (the id of the portal) and userId (the id of the user who crosses), besides type, revision, time and urls, as the PortalActivate schema lists them; its urls name wow/world, which reports the revision.

Joining. Joining is OPTIONAL for a world. A world that states who it is in its World resource (identity, its base URL) MUST also state the claims it asks a visitor for (claims, each claim name marked required or optional) and the credential types it issues (issues, which MAY be empty). A world that states no identity takes no joins, and the rules of this paragraph do not apply to it. A visitor's agent MUST read the World resource from the base URL it is about to post to. Before it discloses anything, it MUST check that identity.base is that base URL. Only then MAY it join with POST /wow/user. The join MUST carry only the claims the world asks for, in a signed manifest, with a holder proof made for this world and this visit. How claims are proven is given by reference. The answer MUST state the outcome (proceed, proceed-in-part or deny) and which of the claims the world asked for were satisfied and which were not. A world MUST record every outcome. The answer MUST NOT grant a permission. Claim values, and anything else about the visitor, MUST NOT appear in a URL. The pointer (the manifest's subject), the signatures, the holder proof and its nonce are made for one world and one visit and MUST NOT be reused for another world; the claim values a world asks for are disclosed to that world.

Following. A page opened at a world's URL with the fragment #follow MUST join that world as a new or existing user, as a page opened at that URL does. The fragment's verb MUST be matched case-insensitively. With #follow=user.{id} the client MUST place the visitor at the node that places that user (User.node) and MUST keep the visitor there while that user moves. When that user is no longer present, the client SHOULD stop following and leave the visitor where it stands.

Departing. DELETE /wow/user/{userId} MUST end that user's visit: afterwards that user MUST no longer be present. A world that offers an event stream MUST send user_left for that user on it, once. The world MUST NOT remove the record of that user's join outcome.

Authorization. A world MAY require a token for its requests. A world that does MUST name its authorization servers in protected resource metadata (RFC 9728) at the address derived from its base URL, {origin}/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource{path prefix}, and a client MUST use that metadata only when its resource equals that base URL. Each token MUST be bound to one world: its audience is the world's base URL (RFC 8707), and a world MUST refuse a token whose audience is not exactly its own base URL, also when the base URL of another world on the same origin starts with its own. A world MUST keep its own grant records. Each names a subject, a scope and the resource it covers, and MAY expire or be withdrawn. A world MUST allow a request only when the token's scopes, and the grant records the world holds for the token's subject when the request arrives, cover it, so that a withdrawn grant refuses the holder's next request. The scope of each request is read for GET and HEAD of the World, User, View, Portal, Spatial and Node resources, observe for the event stream, write for node POST, PUT and DELETE, and enter for joining (POST /wow/user) and leaving (DELETE /wow/user/{userId}, own user only). A write grant MUST name one node, or the whole world, and a write grant on one node MUST NOT cover another node; observe and enter grants MUST cover the whole world. GET /wow/user/{userId} MUST need a read grant that names the world's User resources: a read grant for the rest of the world does not cover them. A world MUST NOT show people to a reader without that grant: user_joined and user_left reach such an observer without user ids, with their revision, and every other path that lists people leaves them out. A request with no token MUST be answered 401 with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer and no error code. An expired token, or a token for another world, MUST be answered 401 with error="invalid_token". A token whose grants do not cover the request MUST be answered 403 with error="insufficient_scope" (RFC 6750, sections 3 and 3.1). The error code MUST be in the WWW-Authenticate header, not only in a body. The 401 answer MUST NOT carry resource_metadata, because RFC 9728, section 3.3 would then require the metadata's resource to equal the request's own URL, which differs from the base URL for every resource below it. On POST /wow/user a 403 with error="insufficient_scope" is that refusal, not a deny. The answer of a join MUST name the scopes granted (JoinAnswer.scope), and they MUST equal the grant records the world holds for that visitor. A world MAY also issue tokens by token exchange (RFC 8693) at its token endpoint: the token of the party acted for is the subject token, a token of the acting party is the actor token, and the issued token is bound to the world as any other. A world MUST issue such a token only when one of its grant records lets the acting party act for that party, and the token MUST carry the act claim, the current actor outermost and each earlier actor nested in it (RFC 8693, section 4.1). For a token with an act claim, a world MUST decide on the grant records of the current actor, not those of the subject, and MUST log the subject and every actor of the chain with each decision. A grant record that lets a party act for another MUST NOT cover the requests that party makes with its own token, so a host that includes a world MUST write into it only with a token that world issued by exchange, with the viewer's token as the subject and the host, named by its base URL, as the actor. A world MUST accept as a subject token only a token of its own authorization server, or of an issuer it lists as trusted whose token names as its audience the world's base URL or the acting party, and MUST refuse any other with error="invalid_request" (RFC 8693, section 2.2.2), also from an issuer it has stopped trusting. On the event stream the token MUST be the first message, as the stream authentication paragraph says, because a browser cannot add a header to a WebSocket. A world MUST close the stream of a holder whose observe grant is withdrawn, or whose token expires, within 5 seconds. A token MUST NOT appear in a URL, and a world MUST NOT accept one there. The token URLs of the oauth2 scheme are relative to the world's base URL, or name the server its metadata gives, since each world names its own authorization server. Outside test environments a world MUST be served over HTTPS. Sender-constrained tokens (DPoP, RFC 9449) are the next step; they are not yet required.

tags.name: canonical
tags.description: Transcribed from the open OpenSpatialWorld spec (WoWAPI@d39a1a0). Where OSL diverges, the operation/schema carries x-osl-divergence and the response is a LABELED extension schema — never a canonical one.

tags.name: osl-extension
tags.description: LABELED OSL addition where the WoW standard is silent. Additive, non-canonical, annotated x-osl-extension, surfaced by conformance.

get.summary: Returns a World status as a single data state.

200.description: world summary (canonical World + labeled OSL extensions)

401.description: no token, or a token that is expired or was issued for another world (WWW-Authenticate)

403.description: the grants of the token do not cover this request (WWW-Authenticate, error insufficient_scope)

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description: ID of user to return (canonical domain is integer).

401.description: no token, or a token that is expired or was issued for another world (WWW-Authenticate)

403.description: the grants of the token do not cover this request (WWW-Authenticate, error insufficient_scope)

delete.description: MUST end the user's visit: afterwards the user MUST no longer be present. A world that offers an event stream MUST send user_left for that user on it, once. The world MUST NOT remove the record of the user's join outcome.

401.description: no token, or a token that is expired or was issued for another world (WWW-Authenticate)

403.description: the grants of the token do not cover this request (WWW-Authenticate, error insufficient_scope)

post.summary: Joins the world as a user, presenting only the claims the world asks for.
post.description: The body MUST carry a signed manifest holding only the claims this world's World resource asks for, and a holder proof made for this world and this visit. The answer is the outcome: proceed, proceed-in-part or deny, with the claims the world asked for that were satisfied and those that were not, each marked required or optional. The world MUST record every outcome. The answer MUST NOT grant a permission. How claims are proven is given by reference; the World API defines no claim format. Claim values, and anything else about the visitor, MUST NOT appear in a URL.

201.description: proceed or proceed-in-part; the visitor is now a User of this world

400.description: the body is not a join

401.description: no token, or a token that is expired or was issued for another world (WWW-Authenticate)

403.description: deny, with the reason and the claims not satisfied

401.description: no token, or a token that is expired or was issued for another world (WWW-Authenticate)

403.description: the grants of the token do not cover this request (WWW-Authenticate, error insufficient_scope)

post.summary: Adds a portal placed by a node, with an optional destination and active radius.

201.description: the portal added (canonical Portal + labeled OSL extensions)

400.description: the body is not a JSON object

401.description: no token, or a token that is expired or was issued for another world (WWW-Authenticate)

403.description: the grants of the token do not cover this request (WWW-Authenticate, error insufficient_scope)

422.description: no node, a node that is not in this world, or an active radius out of range

put.summary: Changes a placed portal's node, destination, label or active radius.

400.description: the body is not a JSON object

401.description: no token, or a token that is expired or was issued for another world (WWW-Authenticate)

403.description: the grants of the token do not cover this request (WWW-Authenticate, error insufficient_scope)

409.description: the portal comes from the world's configuration

422.description: a node that is not in this world, or an active radius out of range

parameters.name: portalId
parameters.description: ID of portal to return (canonical domain is integer).

401.description: no token, or a token that is expired or was issued for another world (WWW-Authenticate)

403.description: the grants of the token do not cover this request (WWW-Authenticate, error insufficient_scope)

get.summary: Returns a Spatial (the graph id, the root node id and the GeoPose anchor of the graph).

parameters.name: spatialID
parameters.description: ID of the spatial composition graph. An integer. OSL also resolves the deprecated string aliases (world id, location id, 'default', 'world').

parameters.name: form
parameters.description: OSL EXTENSION. `descriptor` (default; alias `spatial`) returns the `Spatial`. `node` returns the graph's root node itself, as the canonical `Node` or, with the node form `flat`, as the `OSLFlatNode`. The served form is echoed in the `X-OSL-WoW-Spatial-Form` response header. Equivalent to the request header of the same name, which wins.

parameters.name: X-OSL-WoW-Spatial-Form
parameters.description: The request-header form of the `form` query parameter.

parameters.name: X-OSL-WoW-Node-Form
parameters.description: OSL EXTENSION. With `form=node`: `flat` returns the root as the `OSLFlatNode`; omitted or `canonical` returns the canonical `Node`.

200.description: The `Spatial` by default. With `form=node`, the root node, and the response header `X-OSL-WoW-Spatial-Form` says `node`.

401.description: no token, or a token that is expired or was issued for another world (WWW-Authenticate)

403.description: the grants of the token do not cover this request (WWW-Authenticate, error insufficient_scope)

get.summary: Returns a node of the spatial composition graph, with its whole subtree embedded.

parameters.name: spatialID
parameters.description: ID of the spatial composition graph (an integer; string aliases are deprecated).

parameters.name: X-OSL-WoW-Node-Form
parameters.description: OSL EXTENSION. `flat` returns the node as the `OSLFlatNode` (children are integer ids). Omitted, or `canonical`, returns the canonical `Node`. `?nodeForm=flat` is equivalent.

200.description: The node as the canonical `Node`; the `OSLFlatNode` when the node form is `flat`.

401.description: no token, or a token that is expired or was issued for another world (WWW-Authenticate)

403.description: OSL EXTENSION. The world's read policy refuses this node to this reader (`node_read_refused`); the canonical form of its parent leaves it out.

post.summary: Create and add new child nodes under the given parent node.

parameters.name: spatialID
parameters.description: ID of the spatial composition graph (an integer; string aliases are deprecated).

parameters.name: nodeId
parameters.description: ID of the existing parent node.

parameters.name: X-OSL-WoW-Node-Form
parameters.description: OSL EXTENSION. `flat` means the body is `OSLFlatNode[]` (leaf nodes only) and the response is every node stored, as `OSLFlatNode[]`. Omitted, or `canonical`, means the body is the canonical `Node[]`, whose children may be embedded to any depth; the server assigns every id and returns the nodes the caller sent, with their subtrees and the ids assigned.

requestBody.description: Array of new nodes to add as children of the parent. Canonical `Node[]` by default.

200.description: Successful operation: the created nodes as `Node[]`, ids assigned at every depth. The response header `X-OSL-WoW-Nodes-Stored` reports stored over sent.

400.description: OSL EXTENSION. `invalid_child_entry`, or, in the `flat` form, `child_id_refs_not_supported_on_create`.

401.description: no token, or a token that is expired or was issued for another world (WWW-Authenticate)

403.description: the grants of the token do not cover this request (WWW-Authenticate, error insufficient_scope)

422.description: Validation exception. A body that is not a valid `Node[]` (`node_validation_failed`), a `localTransform` that is not a placement (`invalid_local_transform`: wrong length, a last row other than 0,0,0,1, a number that overflows, or shear), or a graph that would be too deep (`node_tree_too_deep`). Nothing is stored.

put.summary: Update an existing node's content, or move it by setting `parent`.

parameters.name: spatialID
parameters.description: ID of the spatial composition graph (an integer; string aliases are deprecated).

parameters.name: X-OSL-WoW-Node-Form
parameters.description: OSL EXTENSION. `flat` means the body is an `OSLFlatNode`. Omitted, or `canonical`, means a `Node`.

requestBody.description: The updated node. `children` is derived from the tree: a PUT may leave it out or repeat it unchanged, and a PUT whose `children` differ from the stored ones is refused. A PUT of `parent` moves the node, with its subtree, under another node of the same graph.

200.description: Successful operation: the node as the canonical `Node`.

401.description: no token, or a token that is expired or was issued for another world (WWW-Authenticate)

403.description: the grants of the token do not cover this request (WWW-Authenticate, error insufficient_scope)

422.description: Validation exception. `child_restructure_not_supported` (the `children` sent differ from the stored ones), `invalid_local_transform`, or a refused move: `parent_not_found`, `parent_would_create_cycle`, `cannot_move_root`, `invalid_parent`, `node_tree_too_deep`.

delete.summary: Deletes a node and its subtree. Its ids are never issued again within the world.

parameters.name: spatialID
parameters.description: ID of the spatial composition graph (an integer; string aliases are deprecated).

400.description: Invalid node value, or the root, which cannot be deleted.

401.description: no token, or a token that is expired or was issued for another world (WWW-Authenticate)

403.description: the grants of the token do not cover this request (WWW-Authenticate, error insufficient_scope)

worldAuth.description: OAuth 2.0 bearer tokens, each bound to one world, as the Authorization paragraph of the World API describes. The token URL is relative to the world's base URL; a client may instead use the token endpoint of the authorization server that the world's protected resource metadata names.

scopes.read: GET and HEAD of the resources
scopes.enter: joining (POST /wow/user) and leaving (DELETE /wow/user/{userId}, own user only)

IfNoneMatch.name: If-None-Match
IfNoneMatch.description: Entity tags the client holds; a match answers 304 with no body.

IfMatch.name: If-Match
IfMatch.description: The entity tag the change is based on; no match answers 412 and changes nothing.

NotModified.description: Not modified; the client's copy is current.

PreconditionFailed.description: If-Match does not match the node's current entity tag; read the node again and retry.

GeoPose.description: OGC GeoPose 1.0 Basic-YPR. `position` is latitude and longitude in degrees, and `h` in meters above the WGS-84 ellipsoid. `angles` are `yaw`, `pitch` and `roll` in degrees, applied about the local axes z, y and x in that order. A writer MUST send `lon`. A reader MUST also accept `lan`, the earlier spelling, and MUST refuse a position whose `lon` and `lan` differ. A server MUST NOT emit `lan`.

geoPose.description: The world's location, for discovery. It is not a placement: a reader MUST NOT position anything inside the world by it.

spatials.description: The ids of the world's graphs (Spatial resources), the default graph first. A reader MUST treat an absent `spatials` as an empty list.

revision.description: This world's current revision, the count of its changes; each event carries the revision it made.

services.description: The world's services, as URI references relative to its base URL.

preview.description: What a portal leading here shows: an arrival node, a radius and a preview URL, or an image URL, or both. The arrival node, the radius and the preview URL MUST come together. The preview URL MUST return a Node tree rooted at the arrival node. It MUST hold only this world's nodes within the radius of the arrival node, each relative to it, and only those the reader may see. Reading it MUST NOT create a user. URLs are relative to the world's base URL.

radius_m.description: The radius around the arrival node, in meters.

identity.description: Who this world is: the base URL it stands behind. A visitor's agent MUST check that it is the base URL it is about to post to before it discloses anything.

claims.description: The claims this world asks a visitor for when the visitor joins (POST /wow/user), each marked required or optional. A visitor's agent MUST send only these. When issuers is present, the claim MUST count only when one of those issuers signed it. The claim names are provisional.

issues.description: The credential types this world issues. It MAY be empty.

node.description: The node that places the user, relative to the world's base URL. A geoPose given here is derived from that node's placement and MUST equal it.

pilot.description: Who is at the controls, as the visitor stated it when joining: human (a person), agent (software acting alone) or hybrid (a person and software together), or unstated when the join stated none. A world MUST copy it from the join when the join states one, and MUST NOT supply human, agent or hybrid when it does not. For a join without a pilot statement, a world MUST set it to unstated and MUST NOT treat that user as human. A world and a client MUST treat it as the visitor's statement, not as proof of who is at the controls. A client MUST show a user whose pilot is hybrid as an agent wherever it shows that user's name or label. A client MUST show a user whose pilot is unstated as not stated wherever it shows that user's name or label.

node.description: The node that places the view, relative to the world's base URL. A geoPose given here is derived from that node's placement and MUST equal it.

destination.description: The entry URL of the world the portal leads to. Its fragment MAY name where a visitor arrives: #join=node.{id}, a node of that world. Crossing MUST work as navigation to this URL. A portal without a destination leads nowhere: a client MUST NOT cross through it.

node.description: The node that places the portal, relative to the world's base URL. A geoPose given here is derived from that node's placement and MUST equal it.

id.description: A node id MUST be unique within the world, and a server MUST NOT reuse it.

parent.description: The node this one is placed in. Every node MUST have one parent, except the graph's root, which has none. A PUT of `parent` MUST move the node, with its subtree, under another node of the same graph; a server MUST refuse a move under the node itself or its own descendant.

children.description: The child nodes, embedded, derived from the tree. A PUT MAY leave them out or repeat them unchanged. A server MUST NOT change `children` on a PUT, and MUST refuse a PUT whose children differ.

localTransform.description: It MUST be 16 numbers: a column-major 4×4 matrix mapping this node's frame into its parent's frame, in meters. It MUST decompose into translation, rotation and scale, as glTF 2.0 §3.5.3 requires of `node.matrix`, so it has no shear.

spatialAssetURI.description: The address of this node's content. It MAY name a model, or the Spatial, Node or wow/world resource of any world, which is then shown at this node. A client MUST tell them apart by the media type of the answer, never by the address or the content: application/wow+json marks a Web of Worlds resource. The including node stands in for the included node's parent. A whole world shows its default graph, and its other anchored graphs where their GeoPoses put them. The included world's environment MUST NOT apply to the host. The host MUST set a nesting limit and a budget of included graphs, which it hands out in tree order (depth first, children in order). It MUST refuse an inclusion that closes a cycle, detected by URL, and SHOULD show a placeholder on failure. A host MUST read an included part from the part's own world, at its URL, and MUST revalidate it by its entity tag. A copy of that part relayed or embedded by any other world MUST NOT be shown as that part. When the part's own world does not answer, the host SHOULD show the placeholder.

properties.description: Data on the node, as a JSON-LD node object: its "@context" names a context document by URL or gives a context inline, and its "@type", expanded through that context, types the node. The context published beside the world schema (schema/context.jsonld) defines the terms used here; its terms are provisional. A node whose type is wow:Environment belongs, with its subtree, to its world's environment, which does not apply when another world includes it. A property whose value is a URL names data held elsewhere. A data point names one value with a JSON Pointer fragment on the node's URL.

Event.description: A change event on a world's event stream (services.events). Besides the members listed here as required, user_joined carries user, user_left userId, node_created and node_updated node, and node_deleted nodeId.

type.description: user_joined, user_left, node_created, node_updated or node_deleted.

time.description: The server's UTC time of the change, in RFC 3339 form.

urls.description: Every resource whose representation changed, relative to the world's base URL.

PortalActivate.description: The portal_activate event, sent on a world's event stream when a visitor uses a portal: once for each crossing, before the visitor navigates. It is an Event that also names the portal and the user who crosses.

portalId.description: The id of the portal used.

userId.description: The id of the user who crosses.

id.description: The graph's id. It MUST be an integer.

rootNodeID.description: The id of the graph's root node. It MUST be an integer.

extent.description: The box the graph occupies, in meters, in the graph's frame: `min` is its corner with the least x, y and z, and `max` its corner with the greatest. On every axis, `min` MUST NOT exceed `max`. A reader MUST treat an extent whose `min` exceeds `max` as absent.

native_teleportxr_teleport.description: false in this version — no native TeleportXR session teleport.

first_party_teleportxr_browser_rendering.description: false in this version — not first-party TeleportXR rendering.

standards_conformance.description: false on every /wow response — no cosmetic conformance.

target_base_url.description: base URL of the destination world server.

spatial_fabric_address.description: loadable spatial fabric address of the destination.

SpatialFabricSubtree.x-osl-divergence: D8 — the WoW standard has no concept of a node that transcludes a SIGNED, EXECUTABLE spatial document. OpenSpatialAsset is media-type-plural (model/gltf-binary, model/vnd.usdz+zip, ...) but has NO signed-document type. This capability is OURS, labeled, and proposed upstream — it is not granted by the spec.
SpatialFabricSubtree.description: LABELED OSL EXTENSION — carried at `node.webofworlds_extension.spatial_fabric_subtree`. It is the CONTRACT behind the ADDRESS in `Node.spatialAssetURI`, and it is the DISCRIMINATOR: a node is a fabric node iff this member is present. The `.msf` suffix is NEVER sniffed — suffix-sniffing hides exactly the contract this object exists to state. FOUR REQUIRED FIELDS, and every one of them is required for a reason that has already bitten: (a) `unitsPerMeter` has NO DEFAULT. The fabric compositor's `auto` rule is "a fabric whose walk contains celestial nodes composes in AU; any other composes in its native metres". Inherited into a 1:1-metre WoW room, `auto` silently means 1 AU = 1 METRE. That is a defensible reading and a catastrophic default, so it is REFUSED, not defaulted (OSL-FAB-XFORM-1 §3). (b) `upAxis` has NO DEFAULT. The fabric corpus is Z-up; WoW/Three is Y-up. Guess wrong and the solar system lies on its side, silently. An absent or unrecognized `upAxis` is a REFUSAL (OSL-FAB-XFORM-1 §2 — the implementation refuses it, so this contract requires it; a contract that disagreed with its implementation would be the very disease this components is treating). (c) `placement` has NO DEFAULT. It SELECTS THE BACKEND, and the two backends make DIFFERENT HONESTY CLAIMS (see the property description). Defaulting would pick a claim on the author's behalf. (d) `fabricURI` is the signed document itself. NOTHING HERE EARNS A CONFORMANCE FLIP: `standards_conformance` stays `false`. The capability is labeled OSL, declared as divergence D8, surfaced by the conformance components — never disguised as canonical.

fabricURI.description: The signed `.msf` spatial fabric to transclude. NORMALLY IDENTICAL to the node's `spatialAssetURI` (which stays the WoW-native address). Resolved and then VERIFIED fail-closed by the existing `.msf` pipeline (`verifyMsfToken`) — an unverified, unfetchable or tampered fabric is REFUSED with a visible error at EVERY nesting level: never silently dropped, never drawn.

mediaType.description: PROVISIONAL, UNREGISTERED LABEL. `application/msf+jws` is the honest provisional name for a signed, executable spatial document. NO SUCH MEDIA TYPE IS REGISTERED WITH IANA — do not claim otherwise. Registering (or renaming) it is an upstream/MSF question, not ours to settle. Advisory only: it is NOT the discriminator (the presence of this schema is).

unitsPerMeter.description: REQUIRED. NO DEFAULT. EVER. World units per fabric metre (`k` in OSL-FAB-XFORM-1 §3). It is FOLDED INTO THE COMPOSITOR (`composeScale = k * s`, where `s` is the node's decomposed uniform scale) rather than post-multiplied — the engine's own (S·R)² light-intensity rule then applies for free and correctly. Worked example (the demo case): a tabletop orrery with 1 AU = 0.5 m in a 1:1-metre room is `k = 0.5 / 149597870700 = 3.3423e-12`. Omitting this field is a REFUSAL (`MISSING_UNITS_PER_METER`); a non-positive or non-finite value is `BAD_UNITS_PER_METER`.

upAxis.description: REQUIRED. DECLARED, NEVER SNIFFED, NEVER DEFAULTED. `z` = the fabric corpus default (the shared Sneeze UV sphere is Z-up), and the host inserts the fixed basis change B = R_x(-90°) — a pure isometry, determinant +1, so NO GEOMETRY IS RESHAPED. `y` = the fabric is authored Y-up and B = I. An absent or unrecognized value is a REFUSAL (`UNKNOWN_UP_AXIS`), never a fallback to `z` — a fallback would silently reintroduce the exact bug this field exists to kill (OSL-FAB-XFORM-1 §2).

placement.description: REQUIRED. NO DEFAULT. It SELECTS THE BACKEND, and the two backends make DIFFERENT, INCOMPATIBLE HONESTY CLAIMS — so an absent/unknown value is a REFUSAL (`UNKNOWN_PLACEMENT`), never a silent fallback to the flattering backend. `in-room` -> the THREE lowering: ONE scene graph, ONE depth buffer, so an avatar can walk in front of / behind / around the fabric and the occlusion is CORRECT. Shading is APPROXIMATE and it carries **NO PARITY CLAIM, EVER** (`render: "three-approx"`). `backdrop` -> the FILAMENT stacked layer: the measured-parity path (masked SSIM 0.941 vs Artemis's own capture), but it CANNOT DEPTH-COMPOSITE — two stacked WebGL canvases have no shared depth buffer (that is physics, not preference), so NOTHING IN THE ROOM CAN EVER OCCLUDE IT. `artemis.msf` is a backdrop and works perfectly as one; an in-room plinth-mounted fabric would be painter-ordered and an avatar could not walk in front of it.

parallax.description: BACKDROP ONLY. A LABELED dial, 0..1. `0` (the honest default) = orientation-locked: the backdrop follows the camera's rotation but not its translation, which is the truthful behaviour for a layer that has no shared depth buffer. Meaningless for `in-room` (which is genuinely depth-correct and needs no parallax fake).

requireVerified.description: FAIL-CLOSED BY DEFAULT. Absent or `true` => the fabric MUST verify (RS256 + x5c chain to a SHIPPED test anchor) or it is REFUSED and NOT DRAWN, keeping a labeled placeholder and a visible error. `false` is a LABELED local demo ESCAPE HATCH ONLY — it must never be set in a demo or a published world, and a world that sets it cannot claim its subtree is verified. NOTE: "VERIFIED" means a valid signature chaining to a shipped TEST anchor; it is NOT an OS-trust / public-PKI claim.

maxDepth.description: Per-subtree recursion cap for nested child fabrics (a fabric may transclude fabrics). ALWAYS CLAMPED by the engine's absolute MAX_DEPTH — this dial can only ever LOWER the cap, never raise it past the engine's own limit.

epochTicks.description: The epoch at which the fabric's `map.wasm` is run. Fabrics are TIME-DEPENDENT BY DESIGN (orbits move), so the epoch must be STATED rather than implied by wall-clock. This is also why the fabric's internal nodes are NOT projected back up into the WoW graph as addressable WoW nodes: any such projection is a SNAPSHOT AT AN EPOCH, not a graph (deliberately deferred).

UniversalExtensionDeclaration.description: LABELED LAB EXTENSION, carried at `node.webofworlds_extension.universal_extensions` (an array of these). A node is an extension node iff that member is present; the `.wasm` suffix is never the discriminator. When the Lab shows the world, each declaration runs in its own Web Worker, and the scene nodes it makes are drawn under the node that carries it, in that node's frame. A declaration this schema refuses, a module whose SHA-256 differs from `module.integrity`, and a declaration in a world served from another origin are refused before anything runs, with a visible marker labeled with the stage. The standard has no executable node content; `standards_conformance` stays `false`.

url.description: The WebAssembly module, resolved against the world file URL.

integrity.description: The Subresource Integrity form of the SHA-256 of the module bytes. It binds the module to the world file: a module whose hash differs is refused before it is compiled.

binding.description: The import binding the module is built against.

interface.description: The interface the binding implements (`ue:host@0.1.0` for `ue-core/0`, `rp1-sneeze-call` for `rp1-sneeze-call`).

kind.description: The extension attaches to the node that carries it.

requests.description: The capability tokens the extension requests. The host grants a requested token only by its policy: the attachment-confined tokens are granted; a token that needs the user's consent is granted only when the user allows it in the consent dialog.

purposes.description: Why the extension requests a token: a requested token -> its purpose text. The consent dialog shows the text as data, never as markup, and a remembered grant holds only while the purpose is unchanged. A purpose for a token that `requests` does not name is refused at stage `declaration`.

limits.description: Budgets that lower the host budgets, never raise them.

data.description: The data the attachment reads (its `Data`). Absent means an empty object.

glance.description: What the visitor sees before choosing to engage: two short lines, an icon and an action word. The host shows it as plain text, never as markup, and fetches and starts nothing for the extension until the visitor selects the glance (a click, a tap or a keyboard activation; hover, gaze and time in view start nothing). A glance has no rank, priority, bid or order member: the host orders glances itself, nearest first. A declaration without a glance gets one from the host (the node label, then "Extension").

icon.description: An icon name from the host list; a name the host does not know shows its default icon.

hours.description: Opening hours, as data; the host words them itself (for example "until 21:00").

allowed_entry_side.description: named against the portal frame forward axis.

OSLFlatNode.x-osl-divergence: Node.children: integer id-refs (OSL) vs embedded Node objects (canonical)

properties.description: Data on the node, as in the canonical Node.

keyRef.description: did:key DID URL (offline-resolvable; consistency-checked vs the embedded key).

publicKeySpkiB64.description: base64 SPKI DER Ed25519 public key, embedded so the signature verifies without resolving the did:key.

created.description: ISO 8601 (recommended). Lives inside the signature block; excluded from the signing input.

value.description: base64url (unpadded) Ed25519 signature over the JCS-RFC8785 signing input.

signature.description: UMSignature when signed; null on honest unsigned/unverified degradation.

url.description: A JSON file { checkedAt: <date-time>, entries: [{ "@id": <carrier manifest @id>, status: revoked | suspended }] }, ExtensionStatusList.

checkedAt.description: When the place last compiled the list.

UserJoin.description: A join. manifest MUST be a signed manifest that carries only the claims the world asks for. proof MUST be the holder's proof that it controls the manifest's subject, made for this world (its base URL is the audience) and this visit. Their formats are given by reference. pilot, when present, MUST be the visitor's statement of who is at the controls: human, agent or hybrid. A world MUST answer a join whose pilot is present with another value with deny and the reason. A world MUST NOT refuse a join without a pilot statement for that reason alone. It MUST record and show that join as not stated (User.pilot unstated). It MUST NOT treat it as human.

pilot.description: The visitor's pilot statement, human, agent or hybrid, as described above.

JoinAnswer.description: The outcome of a join. A required claim not satisfied MUST give deny. When every required claim is satisfied, an optional claim not satisfied MUST give proceed-in-part. Otherwise the outcome MUST be proceed. Each claim the world asked for MUST be listed once, as satisfied or not satisfied. The answer MUST NOT grant a permission.

trust.description: self-asserted, or issuer-verified when an issuer the world lists for that claim (issuers) signed it. A credential from any other issuer MUST leave the claim self-asserted.

user.description: The User the visitor now is, relative to the world's base URL (not on deny).

scope.description: The scopes the world grants the visitor, space-delimited, each once, from read, observe, write and enter. They MUST equal the grant records the world holds for that visitor. A world that requires no token MAY leave it out.

record.description: LABELED lab extension: where the record of this outcome is read, relative to the base URL.

open_user_manifest_label.description: Honesty label for open_user_manifest (real signature, non-canonical, standards_conformance:false).

node.description: The node that places the portal, relative to the world's base URL (wow/spatial/{g}/node/{n}).

destination.description: The entry URL the portal leads to; null or absent leads nowhere.

active_radius_m.description: The distance, in meters on the floor, at which the portal wakes for a visitor and loads its preview. Above 0 and at most 100. Null or absent: always awake.
The distance at which the portal wakes and loads its preview (placement tool).

placed.description: True for a portal placed with the placement tool, which the tool may move and change; absent for a portal from the world's configuration.
